  • Publishing -- Package and distribute your webview extension

docs.title: Installing Extensions
docs.text: Extensions add languages, debuggers, tools, and other capabilities to DSCode. This guide walks you through every method of discovering and installing extensions.

docs.title: Opening the Extensions View
docs.text:
Open the Extensions view using any of these methods:

  • Press Ctrl+Shift+X (Cmd+Shift+X on macOS)
  • Click the Extensions icon in the Activity Bar on the left side of the window
  • Open the Command Palette with Ctrl+Shift+P and type Extensions: Focus on Extensions View

The Extensions view displays three sections:

  1. Installed -- extensions currently installed in your editor
  2. Recommended -- extensions suggested based on your workspace and usage
  3. Marketplace -- all extensions available from the Open VSX registry

Open VSX Marketplace

DSCode uses the Open VSX marketplace by default rather than the Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace. Open VSX is a vendor-neutral, open-source alternative that hosts thousands of popular extensions. Most well-known extensions are available, but a small number of Microsoft-exclusive extensions (such as Live Share or Remote SSH) may not be present.

docs.title: Searching for Extensions
docs.text:
Type a search term into the text field at the top of the Extensions view to find extensions in the marketplace. Results appear in real time as you type.

DSCode queries the marketplace through the search_marketplace command in the extension_ops module, supporting paginated results with configurable page size.

docs.title: Search Filters
docs.text:
Refine results by prefixing your query with a filter keyword:

Filter Example Description @category: @category:themes Filter by category @sort: @sort:rating Sort results (rating, downloads, name, updated) @installed @installed Show only installed extensions @enabled @enabled Show only enabled extensions @disabled @disabled Show only disabled extensions

You can combine filters:

@category:formatters @sort:downloads prettier

docs.title: Installing an Extension from the Marketplace
docs.text:
1. Find the extension you want in the Extensions view.
  2. Click the Install button next to the extension name.
  3. DSCode downloads the VSIX package from the Open VSX registry and installs it automatically via the install_from_marketplace command.
  4. Some extensions activate immediately; others may require a reload. If a reload is needed, the Install button changes to Reload. Click it to restart the extension host.

Quick install from the Command Palette

Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Extensions: Install Extension, then type the name of the extension you want. Select it from the dropdown to install directly.

docs.title: Installing from a VSIX File
docs.text: You can install an extension manually from a .vsix file. This is useful for extensions not published on the marketplace, pre-release builds, or internal corporate extensions.

docs.title: Method 1 -- Command Palette
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P to open the Command Palette.
  2. Type Install from VSIX and select Extensions: Install from VSIX....
  3. Browse to the .vsix file on your filesystem and select it.
  4. DSCode invokes the install_extension command from extension_ops, which calls install_vsix_package on the session manager.

docs.title: Method 2 -- Drag and Drop
docs.text: Drag a .vsix file from your file manager directly into the DSCode window. DSCode detects the file type and begins installation automatically.

docs.title: Method 3 -- CLI
docs.text:
Install a VSIX from the terminal:

dscode --install-extension path/to/extension.vsix

Additional CLI commands for managing extensions:

# List all installed extensions
dscode --list-extensions

# List installed extensions with versions
dscode --list-extensions --show-versions

# Uninstall an extension by ID
dscode --uninstall-extension publisher.extension-name

# Install a specific version from the marketplace
dscode --install-extension publisher.extension-name@1.2.3

# Disable an extension
dscode --disable-extension publisher.extension-name

Unsigned extensions

VSIX files installed manually bypass marketplace publisher verification. Only install VSIX files from sources you trust.

docs.title: Extension Storage Location
docs.text:
Extensions are stored in platform-specific directories:

Platform Location macOS ~/Library/Application Support/dscode/extensions/ Linux ~/.config/dscode/extensions/ Windows %APPDATA%\dscode\extensions\

Each extension is unpacked into a subdirectory named publisher.extension-name-version/. Extension global state and workspace state are stored separately in the globalStorage/ and workspaceStorage/ subdirectories.

Portable mode

When using the portable version of DSCode, extensions are stored in a data/extensions/ directory relative to the application binary.

docs.title: Network Requirements
docs.text: DSCode needs network access to install extensions from the Open VSX marketplace.

docs.title: Proxy Configuration
docs.text:
If you are behind a corporate proxy, configure it in your settings:

settings.json
{
  "http.proxy": "http://proxy.example.com:8080",
  "http.proxyStrictSSL": true,
  "http.proxyAuthorization": null
}

docs.title: Offline Installation
docs.text:
For air-gapped environments without internet access:

  1. Download the .vsix file on a machine with internet access from open-vsx.org.
  2. Transfer the .vsix file to the target machine via USB, network share, or other means.
  3. Install using any of the VSIX installation methods described above.

docs.title: Firewall Requirements
docs.text:
DSCode connects to the following endpoints for extension management:

Endpoint Purpose https://open-vsx.org Extension search and download https://open-vsx.org/api/ Marketplace REST API

docs.title: Extension Auto-Updates
docs.text:
By default, DSCode checks for extension updates automatically. When an update is available, the MarketplaceUIRegistry emits an marketplace-update-available event and a notification badge appears on the extension in the Extensions view.

You can control auto-update behavior in settings:

settings.json
{
  "extensions.autoUpdate": true,
  "extensions.autoCheckUpdates": true
}
Setting Values Description extensions.autoUpdate true / false Automatically install updates when available extensions.autoCheckUpdates true / false Periodically check the marketplace for updates

To manually check for updates, open the Command Palette with Ctrl+Shift+P and run Extensions: Check for Extension Updates.

Update notifications

DSCode tracks update notifications through the update_notifications system in the MarketplaceUIRegistry. Each notification includes the current version, latest version, and changelog when available.

docs.title: Installing a Specific Version
docs.text:
Sometimes you need a particular version of an extension -- for example, when a new release introduces a regression.

  1. Open the Extensions view with Ctrl+Shift+X.
  2. Find the extension and click the gear icon (:material-cog:) next to it.
  3. Select Install Another Version... from the context menu.
  4. A list of available versions appears. Select the version you need.
  5. DSCode downloads and installs that specific version via install_from_marketplace, passing the chosen version string.
CLI alternative
dscode --install-extension publisher.extension-name@1.2.3

Pinned versions and auto-update

When you install a specific version, DSCode disables auto-update for that extension. To resume receiving updates, reinstall the extension without specifying a version or re-enable auto-update for it.

docs.title: Verifying a Successful Installation
docs.text:
After installation, confirm the extension is active:

  1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. The extension should appear under Installed with a green checkmark.
  3. You can also verify programmatically -- the list_extensions command returns all installed extensions with their metadata.
Example: list_extensions output
{
  "id": "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
  "name": "Prettier - Code formatter",
  "version": "10.4.0",
  "publisher": "esbenp",
  "enabled": true
}

docs.title: Troubleshooting Installation Issues
docs.text:
Extension fails to install
  • Check your internet connection. DSCode must reach https://open-vsx.org to download extensions.
  • If you are behind a corporate proxy, configure the proxy in DSCode settings under http.proxy.
  • Check the Output panel (Ctrl+Shift+U) and select Extensions from the dropdown for error details.
Extension installs but does not activate
  • Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and run Developer: Reload Window.
  • Check the extension's activation events -- some extensions only activate for specific file types or commands.
  • Review the Extension Host log in the Output panel for errors.
VSIX file is invalid or corrupt
  • Verify the file has a .vsix extension and is a valid ZIP archive.
  • Re-download the file from the original source.
  • Ensure the VSIX was built for a compatible VS Code API version.
Extension requires a newer VS Code API version
  • Check the engines.vscode field in the extension's package.json.
  • DSCode currently targets VS Code API level ~1.85.0. Extensions requiring newer API versions may not function correctly.
  • Look for an older version of the extension that is compatible.
Network timeout or connection refused
  • Verify your internet connection and proxy settings (http.proxy in settings).
  • Check that https://open-vsx.org is not blocked by your firewall.
  • Try installing from a .vsix file as a workaround.
Extension activates but features do not work
  • Open the Output panel (Ctrl+Shift+U) and select Extension Host to check for API compatibility errors.
  • The extension may depend on VS Code APIs that are not yet implemented in DSCode. Check the VS Code Compatibility Matrix.
  • File a bug report with the extension name and the specific error from the Extension Host log.

docs.title: Managing Extensions
docs.text: Once extensions are installed, DSCode provides a full set of tools for managing their lifecycle -- enabling, disabling, configuring, and removing extensions as your workflow evolves.

docs.title: Viewing Installed Extensions
docs.text:
Open the Extensions view by pressing Ctrl+Shift+X and look under the Installed section. Each entry shows:

  • Extension name and publisher
  • Installed version
  • A brief description
  • Current state (enabled, disabled, or needs update)

You can also list all installed extensions from the Command Palette:

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P.
  2. Run Extensions: Show Installed Extensions.

Under the hood, the list_extensions command in the extension_ops module calls list_extensions_detailed() on the session manager, returning full metadata for every installed extension.

docs.title: Filtering Installed Extensions
docs.text:
Use the search field with these filter prefixes:

Filter Description @installed All installed extensions @enabled Only enabled extensions @disabled Only disabled extensions @outdated Extensions with available updates

docs.title: Enabling and Disabling Extensions
docs.text: Disabling an extension stops it from running without removing it. This is useful for troubleshooting conflicts or reducing resource usage.

docs.title: Disable an Extension Globally
docs.text:
1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. Click the gear icon (:material-cog:) on the extension you want to disable.
  3. Select Disable.
  4. The extension stops running immediately or after a reload.

docs.title: Disable an Extension for the Current Workspace Only
docs.text:
1. Click the gear icon (:material-cog:) on the extension.
  2. Select Disable (Workspace).
  3. The extension remains active in all other workspaces but is disabled in the current one.

Workspace-scoped disabling

Workspace-level disabling is stored in .dscode/settings.json within your project folder. This setting can be committed to version control so that all team members share the same extension state for the project.

docs.title: Re-enable an Extension
docs.text:
1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. Find the disabled extension (it will have a greyed-out icon).
  3. Click the gear icon (:material-cog:) and select Enable or Enable (Workspace).

docs.title: Uninstalling Extensions
docs.text:
1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. Click the gear icon (:material-cog:) next to the extension.
  3. Select Uninstall.
  4. DSCode calls the uninstall_extension command, which invokes delete_extension on the session manager to remove the extension files from disk.

You can also uninstall from the command line:

dscode --uninstall-extension publisher.extension-name

Uninstall is permanent

Uninstalling removes the extension and all its files from the extensions directory. Your extension settings in settings.json are preserved, so if you reinstall the extension later, your configuration is restored automatically.

docs.title: Extension Settings
docs.text: Most extensions expose configurable settings. There are several ways to access them.

docs.title: From the Extensions View
docs.text:
1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. Click the gear icon (:material-cog:) on the extension.
  3. Select Extension Settings.
  4. DSCode opens the Settings editor, filtered to show only that extension's settings.

docs.title: From the Settings Editor
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+, to open Settings.
  2. Search for the extension name or a specific setting key.
  3. Modify values as needed.

docs.title: Editing settings.json Directly
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON) to edit your configuration file directly:

settings.json
{
  "prettier.tabWidth": 4,
  "prettier.singleQuote": true,
  "eslint.validate": ["javascript", "typescript", "svelte"]
}

Settings follow a hierarchy with increasing specificity:

  1. Default -- the extension's built-in defaults
  2. User -- your global settings (~/.config/dscode/settings.json)
  3. Workspace -- project-level overrides (.dscode/settings.json)
  4. Folder -- per-folder overrides in multi-root workspaces

docs.title: Extension Runtime Information
docs.text:
To inspect runtime details of a running extension:

  1. Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).
  2. Run Developer: Show Running Extensions.
  3. DSCode displays a list of all active extensions with:
    • Activation time (milliseconds)
    • Status (activated, activating, or inactive)
    • Activation event that triggered the extension

The get_extension_contributions command from extension_ops retrieves detailed contribution data, including commands, menus, keybindings, and views registered by each extension.

Performance profiling

If an extension is causing slowdowns, look at its activation time and status. Extensions that take more than 500ms to activate are flagged with a warning icon. You can disable slow extensions to improve editor startup time.

docs.title: Recommended Extensions for a Workspace
docs.text: You can define a set of extensions that are recommended for anyone working in your project. This is useful for teams to ensure consistent tooling.

docs.title: Creating the Recommendations File
docs.text:
Create a file at .dscode/extensions.json in your workspace root:

.dscode/extensions.json
{
  "recommendations": [
    "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
    "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
    "svelte.svelte-vscode",
    "rust-lang.rust-analyzer"
  ],
  "unwantedRecommendations": [
    "some-publisher.conflicting-extension"
  ]
}
Field Description recommendations Array of extension IDs that DSCode will suggest to install when the workspace is opened unwantedRecommendations Array of extension IDs that should not be recommended for this workspace

When a team member opens the project, DSCode displays a notification:

This workspace has extension recommendations. Would you like to install them?

They can choose to install all, review the list, or dismiss.

Commit this file

Add .dscode/extensions.json to version control. This ensures every contributor gets the same recommendations when they clone the project.

docs.title: Detecting Conflicts
docs.text:
Some extensions provide overlapping functionality, which can cause unexpected behavior. Common conflicts include:

  • Multiple formatters for the same language (e.g., Prettier and Beautify both formatting JavaScript)
  • Competing linters with conflicting rules
  • Multiple color themes trying to apply simultaneously

DSCode detects some conflicts automatically and shows a warning in the Extensions view.

docs.title: Resolving Conflicts
General Troubleshooting Steps
docs.text:
An extension stopped working after an update
  1. Check the extension's changelog for breaking changes.
  2. Try disabling and re-enabling the extension.
  3. If the issue persists, install the previous version (see Installing a Specific Version).
  4. Report the issue to the extension publisher.
Extensions panel shows 'Error loading extensions'
  1. Check your network connection -- the MarketplaceUIRegistry needs to reach the Open VSX API.
  2. Open the Output panel (Ctrl+Shift+U) and select Extensions for detailed error messages.
  3. Try running Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).
Extension host crashed

The extension host runs in a separate process. If it crashes:

  1. DSCode automatically attempts to restart it.
  2. If it continues to crash, open the Command Palette and run Developer: Show Extension Host Log.
  3. Identify the problematic extension and disable it.
  4. Restart DSCode to restore a clean extension host state.
How do I reset all extension state?

Use the clear_marketplace_data command to reset the marketplace UI registry, or manually delete the extensions directory:

# Location varies by platform
# Linux:   ~/.config/dscode/extensions/
# macOS:   ~/Library/Application Support/dscode/extensions/
# Windows: %APPDATA%\dscode\extensions\

docs.title: Extension Marketplace
docs.text: The DSCode marketplace is your gateway to thousands of extensions that enhance the editor with new languages, themes, debuggers, and tools. DSCode connects to the Open VSX registry, providing a vendor-neutral and open-source extension ecosystem.

docs.title: Browsing the Marketplace
docs.text:
Open the marketplace from within DSCode:

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+X to open the Extensions view.
  2. The Marketplace section displays featured and popular extensions.
  3. Type in the search bar to find specific extensions.

The marketplace UI is powered by the MarketplaceUIRegistry and marketplace_ui_ops modules on the Rust backend, which manage featured extensions, categories, reviews, ratings, and search results. Queries are executed through the search_marketplace command in extension_ops, which supports pagination and configurable result sizes.

Open VSX Registry

DSCode uses Open VSX as its default extension registry. Open VSX is an open-source, vendor-neutral marketplace for VS Code extensions, maintained by the Eclipse Foundation. Most popular extensions are available, and publishers can easily add their extensions to the registry.

docs.title: Category Filters
docs.text:
The marketplace organizes extensions into categories so you can browse by type. The MarketplaceUIRegistry provides these built-in categories:

Category Description Filter syntax Programming Languages Language support and syntax highlighting @category:programming-languages Themes Color themes and icon themes @category:themes Snippets Code snippets and templates @category:snippets Debuggers Debugging support for various languages @category:debuggers Formatters Code formatting tools @category:formatters Linters Code quality and linting tools @category:linters Keymaps Keyboard shortcuts and keybindings @category:keymaps Other Extensions that don't fit other categories @category:other

To browse a specific category, type the filter prefix in the search bar:

@category:themes

You can combine a category filter with a search term:

@category:formatters python

docs.title: Sorting Results
docs.text:
Control the order of search results using the @sort: filter or the sort dropdown in the Extensions view. DSCode supports the following sort modes, corresponding to the SortBy enum in the backend:

Sort Option Filter Syntax Description Relevance @sort:relevance Best match for your search query (default) Rating @sort:rating Highest average user rating first Downloads @sort:downloads Most downloaded extensions first Name @sort:name Alphabetical order Updated @sort:updated Most recently updated first

Example -- find the most downloaded Python linters:

@category:linters @sort:downloads python

docs.title: Extension Details Page
docs.text: Click on any extension in the marketplace list to open its details page. The details page includes several tabs:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Description -- the publisher's full description of what the extension does, often with feature lists and screenshots
  • Publisher name -- who maintains the extension, with a link to their other extensions
  • Install count -- total number of installations
  • Rating -- average star rating and total number of reviews
  • Version -- the current published version
  • Last updated -- date of the most recent release
  • Repository link -- link to the source code (if provided)

docs.title: Screenshots and Media
docs.text: Publishers can embed screenshots, GIFs, and feature highlight images in the extension description. These render directly in the details view so you can see the extension in action before installing.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
The Changelog tab shows a version-by-version history of changes. When the MarketplaceUIRegistry tracks an update notification, it stores the changelog text alongside version information:

Update notification structure
{
  "extensionId": "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
  "extensionName": "Prettier - Code formatter",
  "currentVersion": "10.3.0",
  "latestVersion": "10.4.0",
  "changeLog": "## 10.4.0\n- Added support for Svelte 5 syntax\n- Fixed formatting regression in template literals",
  "createdAt": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Some extensions depend on other extensions to function. The dependencies section lists:

  • Extension Pack members -- for extension packs, all included extensions are listed
  • Required dependencies -- extensions that must be installed for this extension to work
  • Optional dependencies -- extensions that enhance functionality but are not required

DSCode automatically installs required dependencies when you install an extension.

Extension packs

An extension pack is a collection of extensions bundled under a single install action. Installing a pack installs all member extensions. Uninstalling the pack does not automatically remove member extensions.

docs.title: Publisher Verification
docs.text: The marketplace displays verification status to help you assess extension trustworthiness.

docs.title: Verification Indicators
docs.text: Indicator Meaning :material-check-decagram:{ .verified } Verified The publisher's identity has been confirmed by the Open VSX registry No badge The publisher has not completed identity verification

docs.title: Assessing Extension Trust
docs.text:
Before installing an extension, consider:

  • Is the publisher verified?
  • Does the extension have a significant number of downloads?
  • Are the ratings and reviews positive?
  • Is the source code available and open-source?
  • When was the extension last updated?

Security considerations

Extensions run with the same permissions as DSCode itself. A malicious extension could read your files, access the network, or execute arbitrary code. Always review the extension's permissions, source code (if available), and community feedback before installing.

docs.title: Ratings and Reviews
docs.text: The marketplace includes a ratings and reviews system managed by the MarketplaceUIRegistry.

docs.title: Viewing Ratings
docs.text:
Each extension displays an aggregate rating:

  • Average rating -- calculated from all user reviews (1 to 5 stars)
  • Total ratings -- the number of users who have rated the extension
  • Rating distribution -- breakdown showing how many users gave each star level

The backend stores this as an ExtensionRating struct:

Rating structure (from marketplace_ui_registry)
pub struct ExtensionRating {
    pub average_rating: f64,
    pub total_ratings: usize,
    pub rating_distribution: HashMap<u8, usize>,
}

docs.title: Reading Reviews
docs.text:
Click the Reviews tab on an extension's details page to read user reviews. Reviews are paginated for performance -- the get_extension_reviews_paginated command fetches reviews in configurable page sizes.

Each review includes:

  • Author -- the reviewer's display name
  • Star rating -- 1 to 5 stars
  • Title -- a short summary (optional)
  • Comment -- detailed feedback (optional)
  • Date -- when the review was posted
  • Helpful count -- how many users found the review useful

docs.title: Leaving a Review
docs.text:
1. Open the extension details page.
  2. Click the Write a Review button.
  3. Select a star rating (1-5).
  4. Optionally add a title and comment.
  5. Submit your review.

Helpful reviews

The best reviews explain specific use cases, mention pros and cons, and note the language or framework context. These help other developers make informed decisions.

docs.title: Marketplace Search Tips
docs.text:
Here are some effective ways to search the marketplace:

By exact IDBy functionalityBy category and sortBy installed state 
esbenp.prettier-vscode

Use the full publisher.extension-name format to find an exact extension.

python formatter

Describe what you need and DSCode finds matching extensions.

@category:themes @sort:rating dark

Combine filters to narrow down to highly-rated dark themes.

@installed @outdated

Find installed extensions that have updates available.

docs.title: Recommended Extensions
docs.text:
This curated list highlights extensions that work well with DSCode across common languages and workflows. All recommendations are available on the Open VSX marketplace. Install any of them by pressing Ctrl+Shift+X and searching for the extension ID.

Quick install

Copy the extension ID (e.g., dbaeumer.vscode-eslint) and paste it into the Extensions search bar to find and install the extension instantly.

docs.title: Web Development
docs.text: Extensions for building web applications with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and modern frameworks.

docs.title: ESLint
docs.text:
dbaeumer.vscode-eslint

Integrates ESLint into DSCode, providing real-time JavaScript and TypeScript linting as you type. Highlights problems in your code, suggests fixes, and can auto-fix on save. Supports custom rule configurations and popular presets like Airbnb and Standard.

Recommended settings
{
  "eslint.validate": ["javascript", "typescript", "svelte", "html"],
  "editor.codeActionsOnSave": {
    "source.fixAll.eslint": true
  }
}

docs.title: Prettier -- Code Formatter
docs.text:
esbenp.prettier-vscode

An opinionated code formatter that enforces a consistent style across your entire codebase. Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, JSON, Markdown, YAML, and many more languages. Eliminates debates about code style in team projects.

Recommended settings
{
  "editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
  "editor.formatOnSave": true
}

docs.title: HTML CSS Support
docs.text:
ecmel.vscode-html-css

Provides CSS class name completion for HTML class attributes. Scans your stylesheets (including linked CSS files, inline styles, and CSS modules) and offers IntelliSense autocomplete when writing class names in HTML and template files.

docs.title: Live Server
docs.text:
ritwickdey.liveserver

Launches a local development server with live reload. When you save an HTML, CSS, or JavaScript file, your browser automatically refreshes to show the latest changes. Ideal for rapid prototyping and front-end development without a build step.

docs.title: Python
docs.text: Extensions for Python development, from scripting to data science.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
ms-python.python

The essential Python extension. Provides IntelliSense (via Pylance or Jedi), linting, debugging, code navigation, refactoring, testing support, and Jupyter notebook integration. Automatically detects virtual environments, conda, and pyenv installations.

docs.title: Pylance
docs.text:
ms-python.vscode-pylance

A high-performance Python language server built on Pyright. Delivers fast type checking, auto-imports, semantic highlighting, and rich IntelliSense. Significantly faster than the default Jedi-based language server for large codebases.

Pylance and the Python extension

Pylance works alongside the Python extension. Install both for the best Python development experience in DSCode.

docs.title: Jupyter
docs.text:
ms-toolsai.jupyter

Run Jupyter notebooks directly inside DSCode. Provides interactive cell execution, inline plots and visualizations, variable explorer, and kernel management. Supports Python, R, Julia, and other Jupyter kernels.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text: Extensions for the Rust programming language, particularly relevant since DSCode's own backend is built with Rust and Tauri.

docs.title: rust-analyzer
docs.text:
rust-lang.rust-analyzer

The official Rust language server. Provides code completion, go-to-definition, find references, type hover information, inline error diagnostics, code actions, and refactoring support. Understands Cargo workspaces, procedural macros, and the Rust trait system.

Recommended settings
{
  "rust-analyzer.check.command": "clippy",
  "rust-analyzer.inlayHints.parameterHints.enable": true,
  "rust-analyzer.inlayHints.typeHints.enable": true
}

Building DSCode from source?

If you are contributing to DSCode itself, rust-analyzer is essential for navigating the Tauri backend codebase. It understands the #[tauri::command] macros and provides IntelliSense across the IPC boundary.

docs.title: JavaScript / TypeScript
docs.text: Extensions for enhanced JavaScript and TypeScript development beyond what the built-in language support provides.

docs.title: TypeScript Language Features
docs.text: Built into DSCode -- no installation required. Provides IntelliSense, refactoring, go-to-definition, and error checking for TypeScript and JavaScript files. DSCode bundles the TypeScript language service via the Monaco editor.

docs.title: ES7+ React/Redux/React-Native Snippets
docs.text:
dsznajder.es7-react-js-snippets

A collection of code snippets for React, Redux, and React Native development. Type short prefixes to expand into full component boilerplate, hooks patterns, Redux actions, and more.

Prefix Expands to rafce React Arrow Function Component with Export useState useState hook with state and setter useEffect useEffect hook with cleanup function rcc React Class Component

docs.title: Git
docs.text: Extensions that supercharge DSCode's built-in Git support.

docs.title: GitLens
docs.text:
eamodio.gitlens

Adds rich Git capabilities directly into the editor. Shows inline blame annotations on every line, provides a visual file history, lets you compare branches and commits side by side, and offers a powerful search across your repository history.

Key features:

  • Current line blame -- see who last modified the line you are on, and when
  • File history view -- browse every commit that touched the current file
  • Commit graph -- visualize branch topology and merge history
  • Interactive rebase editor -- reorder, squash, and edit commits visually

docs.title: Git Graph
docs.text:
mhutchie.git-graph

Displays your Git repository history as a clean, interactive graph. Visualize branches, merges, and tags. Right-click any commit to cherry-pick, revert, create a branch, or reset. Useful for understanding complex branch histories at a glance.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text: Color themes and icon themes to customize the look of your editor.

docs.title: One Dark Pro
docs.text:
zhuangtongfa.material-theme

A faithful port of Atom's iconic One Dark theme. Provides a dark color scheme with carefully chosen syntax highlighting colors that reduce eye strain during long coding sessions. One of the most popular themes across all editors.

docs.title: Dracula Official
docs.text:
dracula-theme.theme-dracula

A dark theme with vibrant, high-contrast colors. The purple-accented palette is distinctive and easy to read. Supports consistent theming across dozens of development tools beyond just the editor.

docs.title: Material Icon Theme
docs.text:
pkief.material-icon-theme

Replaces the default file and folder icons in the explorer with Material Design icons. Provides unique icons for hundreds of file types, frameworks, and tools, making it easy to identify files at a glance in the sidebar.

docs.title: Productivity
docs.text: General-purpose extensions that improve your daily editing workflow.

docs.title: TODO Highlight
docs.text:
wayou.vscode-todo-highlight

Highlights TODO, FIXME, HACK, and other comment annotations in your code with configurable colors. Makes it easy to spot incomplete work and technical debt at a glance. Supports custom keywords and colors.

Example custom keywords
{
  "todohighlight.keywords": [
    { "text": "TODO:", "color": "#fff", "backgroundColor": "#ffbd2a" },
    { "text": "FIXME:", "color": "#fff", "backgroundColor": "#f06292" },
    { "text": "NOTE:", "color": "#fff", "backgroundColor": "#64b5f6" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Bracket Pair Colorizer
docs.text:
Built into DSCode -- enable it in settings. Colors matching brackets with the same color, making it easy to identify scope boundaries in deeply nested code.

Enable native bracket colorization
{
  "editor.bracketPairColorization.enabled": true,
  "editor.guides.bracketPairs": "active"
}

Built-in feature

Bracket pair colorization was originally a popular extension but is now a built-in feature of the Monaco editor. No separate installation is needed -- just enable it in settings.

docs.title: Path Intellisense
docs.text:
christian-kohler.path-intellisense

Autocompletes file paths as you type them in your code. Works in import statements, require calls, HTML src attributes, CSS url() functions, and configuration files. Saves time and eliminates typos in file references.

docs.title: Workspace Recommendations File
docs.text:
To recommend a set of these extensions for your team, create a .dscode/extensions.json file in your project root:

Web project (Svelte)Python data scienceRust projectFull-stack (TypeScript + Rust) .dscode/extensions.json
{
  "recommendations": [
    "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
    "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
    "svelte.svelte-vscode",
    "ecmel.vscode-html-css",
    "eamodio.gitlens",
    "christian-kohler.path-intellisense",
    "wayou.vscode-todo-highlight"
  ]
}
.dscode/extensions.json
{
  "recommendations": [
    "ms-python.python",
    "ms-python.vscode-pylance",
    "ms-toolsai.jupyter",
    "eamodio.gitlens",
    "wayou.vscode-todo-highlight"
  ]
}
.dscode/extensions.json
{
  "recommendations": [
    "rust-lang.rust-analyzer",
    "eamodio.gitlens",
    "mhutchie.git-graph",
    "wayou.vscode-todo-highlight",
    "christian-kohler.path-intellisense"
  ]
}
.dscode/extensions.json
{
  "recommendations": [
    "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
    "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
    "rust-lang.rust-analyzer",
    "eamodio.gitlens",
    "mhutchie.git-graph",
    "christian-kohler.path-intellisense",
    "pkief.material-icon-theme"
  ]
}

See Managing Extensions -- Recommended Extensions for details on how workspace recommendations work.

docs.title: Your First Project
docs.text:
In this tutorial you will build a small web page from scratch using DSCode. Along the way you will use the editor, the integrated terminal, extensions, and Git integration -- the core workflows that make DSCode productive for real-world development.

Time required: ~15 minutes

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Project Directory
docs.text:
Open your system terminal (or the DSCode integrated terminal if DSCode is already running) and create a new directory:

mkdir ~/my-first-project
cd ~/my-first-project

docs.title: Step 2: Open the Project in DSCode
docs.text:
Open the folder in DSCode using one of these methods:

TerminalMenuKeyboard 
dscode ~/my-first-project

In DSCode, go to File > Open Folder... and select my-first-project.

Press Ctrl+O (Cmd+O on macOS) and navigate to the folder.

The Explorer sidebar should now show an empty project.

docs.title: Step 3: Create Your Files
docs.text: You will create three files: an HTML page, a CSS stylesheet, and a JavaScript file.

docs.title: index.html
docs.text:
1. In the Explorer sidebar, click the New File icon (or press Ctrl+N / Cmd+N).
  2. Name the file index.html.
  3. Type ! and press Tab to expand the Emmet abbreviation into a full HTML5 boilerplate.

Emmet in action

DSCode includes Emmet support out of the box. Try typing ul>li*5>a{Item $} and pressing Tab -- it expands into a full unordered list with five linked items.

Replace the contents of <body> with:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>My First DSCode Project</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css" />
</head>
<body>
    <div class="container">
        <h1>Hello from DSCode!</h1>
        <p id="message">Click the button to get started.</p>
        <button id="action-btn">Click Me</button>
    </div>
    <script src="app.js"></script>
</body>
</html>

Save the file with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS).

docs.title: style.css
docs.text:
Create a new file called style.css and add:

* {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    box-sizing: border-box;
}

body {
    font-family: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: center;
    align-items: center;
    min-height: 100vh;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea, #764ba2);
    color: #fff;
}

.container {
    text-align: center;
    padding: 2rem;
}

h1 {
    font-size: 2.5rem;
    margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

p {
    font-size: 1.2rem;
    margin-bottom: 2rem;
    opacity: 0.9;
}

button {
    padding: 0.75rem 2rem;
    font-size: 1rem;
    border: 2px solid #fff;
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: transparent;
    color: #fff;
    cursor: pointer;
    transition: all 0.2s ease;
}

button:hover {
    background: #fff;
    color: #764ba2;
}

docs.title: app.js
docs.text:
Create a new file called app.js and add:

const button = document.getElementById("action-btn");
const message = document.getElementById("message");

let clickCount = 0;

button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    clickCount++;
    message.textContent = `You clicked ${clickCount} time${clickCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}!`;
});

docs.title: Step 4: Explore Editor Features
docs.text: Now that you have three files open, try out some of the editing features that make DSCode powerful.

docs.title: IntelliSense
docs.text:
Open app.js and start typing document.query. DSCode will show autocomplete suggestions powered by the Monaco editor's built-in JavaScript/TypeScript language service.

  • Press Enter or Tab to accept a suggestion.
  • Press Esc to dismiss the autocomplete menu.
  • Press Ctrl+Space (Cmd+Space on macOS) to manually trigger suggestions at any time.

docs.title: Multi-Cursor Editing
docs.text:
1. Open style.css.
  2. Select the word margin on any line.
  3. Press Ctrl+D (Cmd+D on macOS) repeatedly to select the next occurrence.
  4. Type a replacement -- all cursors update simultaneously.

Alternatively, hold Alt (Option on macOS) and click at multiple positions to place cursors manually.

docs.title: Emmet Abbreviations
docs.text:
Open index.html, place your cursor inside <div class="container">, and try typing:

p.description{This is a new paragraph}

Press Tab to expand it into:

<p class="description">This is a new paragraph</p>

docs.title: Step 5: Run a Local Server
docs.text:
Open the integrated terminal with Ctrl+` (Cmd+` on macOS).

If you have Python installed, start a quick HTTP server:

Python 3Node.js (npx)PHP 
python3 -m http.server 8080

npx serve -l 8080

php -S localhost:8080

Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser to see your page in action. Click the button to verify the JavaScript is working.

Live reload

For a better development experience, install a live-reload server:

npm install -g live-server
live-server --port=8080

Changes you save in DSCode will automatically refresh the browser.

docs.title: Step 6: Install an Extension
docs.text:
Let us install an extension to improve the development workflow.

  1. Open the Extensions sidebar with Ctrl+Shift+X (Cmd+Shift+X on macOS).
  2. Search for Live Preview.
  3. Click Install.

Once installed, you can right-click index.html in the Explorer and select Open with Live Preview to see a real-time preview inside DSCode.

Recommended extensions for web development

  • Prettier -- Automatic code formatting
  • ESLint -- JavaScript linting
  • Auto Rename Tag -- Rename matching HTML tags
  • CSS Peek -- Jump to CSS definitions from HTML

See Recommended Extensions for a curated list.

docs.title: Step 7: Initialize Git and Make Your First Commit
docs.text: DSCode has built-in Git integration. Let us set up version control for this project.

docs.title: Initialize the Repository
docs.text:
Open the integrated terminal (Ctrl+` / Cmd+`) and run:

git init

You will notice the Explorer sidebar now shows file status indicators -- untracked files appear with a U badge.

docs.title: Stage Your Files
docs.text:
You can stage files in two ways:

Source Control PanelTerminal
  1. Click the Source Control icon in the activity bar (or press Ctrl+Shift+G / Cmd+Shift+G).
  2. Hover over each file under Changes and click the + icon to stage it.
  3. Or click the + next to the Changes header to stage all files at once.
git add -A

docs.title: Commit
docs.text:
1. In the Source Control panel, type a commit message in the text field at the top:

    Initial commit: add HTML, CSS, and JS files

  2. Press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) or click the Commit button.

Git configuration

If this is your first time using Git, you may need to configure your identity:

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

docs.title: View History
docs.text: Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P) and type Git: View History to see your commit log.

docs.title: What You Learned
docs.text:
In this tutorial you covered the fundamental DSCode workflows:

  • Creating and opening a project
  • Creating and editing files with syntax highlighting
  • Using IntelliSense for autocomplete
  • Multi-cursor editing for efficient changes
  • Emmet abbreviations for rapid HTML authoring
  • Running commands in the integrated terminal
  • Installing extensions to enhance functionality
  • Initializing a Git repository, staging, and committing

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
You now have a solid foundation. Here are some areas to explore next:

  • Editor Features -- Deep dive into code navigation, refactoring, snippets, and more.
  • Integrated Terminal -- Split terminals, shell profiles, and task automation.
  • Git Integration -- Branching, merging, diff viewing, and remote workflows.
  • Search -- Project-wide search and replace with regex support.
  • Settings and Configuration -- Customize DSCode to match your preferences.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts -- Master the shortcuts that will make you faster.
  • Installing Extensions -- Browse the marketplace and manage your extension library.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide covers everything you need to build and run DSCode from source on macOS, Linux, or Windows.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have the following installed:

Dependency Minimum Version Purpose Rust 1.70+ Tauri backend and native modules Node.js 18+ Frontend build tooling npm 9+ Package management Git 2.30+ Cloning the repository

Why build from source?

DSCode is in active development. Pre-built binaries will be available once the project reaches a stable release. For now, building from source is the recommended way to run DSCode.

docs.title: Platform-Specific Dependencies
docs.text: macOSLinuxWindows

docs.title: Xcode Command Line Tools
docs.text:
Install the Xcode CLI tools, which provide clang, make, and other essential build utilities:

xcode-select --install

docs.title: System Libraries
docs.text:
Install the required system libraries with Homebrew:

brew install cmake pkg-config openssl@3

Apple Silicon

DSCode supports both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs natively. The build system will automatically detect your architecture.

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    wget \
    file \
    libssl-dev \
    libgtk-3-dev \
    libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
    librsvg2-dev \
    libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
    libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev \
    libsoup-3.0-dev \
    pkg-config

docs.title: Fedora / RHEL
docs.text:
sudo dnf install -y \
    gcc gcc-c++ make cmake \
    openssl-devel \
    gtk3-devel \
    libappindicator-gtk3-devel \
    librsvg2-devel \
    webkit2gtk4.1-devel \
    javascriptcoregtk4.1-devel \
    libsoup3-devel \
    pkg-config

docs.title: Arch Linux
docs.text:
sudo pacman -S --needed \
    base-devel \
    curl wget file \
    openssl \
    gtk3 \
    libappindicator-gtk3 \
    librsvg \
    webkit2gtk-4.1 \
    pkg-config

Wayland Support

DSCode runs on both X11 and Wayland. If you are on a Wayland-only session, make sure webkit2gtk was compiled with Wayland support. Most distribution packages include it by default.

docs.title: Visual Studio Build Tools
docs.text: Download and install the Visual Studio Build Tools. During installation, select the "Desktop development with C++" workload. This provides MSVC, CMake, and the Windows SDK.

docs.title: WebView2 Runtime
docs.text:
DSCode uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 for its webview layer. Windows 10 (version 1803+) and Windows 11 typically have it pre-installed. If not, download it from the WebView2 download page.

You can verify it is installed by running:

Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\Clients\{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BEB-E15811B4C70D}" -Name pv

docs.title: Rust on Windows
docs.text:
Install Rust through rustup. During setup, choose the MSVC toolchain (default on Windows):

winget install Rustlang.Rustup

Windows Subsystem for Linux

You can also build DSCode inside WSL 2. Follow the Linux tab instructions inside your WSL distribution and install an X server or use WSLg for GUI output.

docs.title: Install Rust (All Platforms)
docs.text:
If you do not already have Rust installed, use rustup:

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

After installation, verify your version:

rustc --version   # should be 1.70 or higher
cargo --version

docs.title: Install the Tauri CLI
docs.text:
The Tauri CLI drives the build and development workflow:

cargo install tauri-cli

Verify the installation:

cargo tauri --version

Alternative: npx

You can also run the Tauri CLI through npx without a global install:

npx @tauri-apps/cli dev

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/nicepkg/dscode.git
cd dscode

docs.title: 2. Install Node Dependencies
docs.text: npm install

docs.title: 3. Run in Development Mode
docs.text:
npm run tauri dev

This will:

  1. Start the Svelte dev server with hot-reload.
  2. Compile the Rust backend.
  3. Launch the DSCode window.

The first build takes several minutes while Cargo downloads and compiles dependencies. Subsequent builds are significantly faster thanks to incremental compilation.

docs.title: 4. Build a Release Binary
docs.text:
To create an optimized, distributable binary:

npm run tauri build
macOSLinuxWindows

The output is a .app bundle and a .dmg installer located in:

src-tauri/target/release/bundle/dmg/

The output includes .deb and .AppImage packages in:

src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/
src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/

The output is an .msi installer and a portable .exe in:

src-tauri\target\release\bundle\msi\
src-tauri\target\release\bundle\nsis\

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After launching DSCode, verify everything is working:

  1. Window appears -- The DSCode editor window opens without errors.
  2. Open a folder -- Use Ctrl+O (or Cmd+O on macOS) to open any project folder.
  3. Edit a file -- Open a file and confirm syntax highlighting and IntelliSense are active.
  4. Open the terminal -- Press Ctrl+` to open the integrated terminal and run a command.
  5. Check the command palette -- Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or Cmd+Shift+P on macOS) and type About to view version information.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Rust compilation is very slow on the first build

The initial build compiles the entire Rust dependency tree. This is expected and can take 5--10 minutes depending on your hardware. Use cargo install sccache and set RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache to cache compilation artifacts across builds:

cargo install sccache
export RUSTC_WRAPPER="sccache"
npm run tauri dev
npm install fails with permission errors

Avoid running npm with sudo. Instead, configure npm to use a user-level directory:

mkdir -p ~/.npm-global
npm config set prefix '~/.npm-global'
export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"

Add the export line to your shell profile (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, etc.) to make it permanent.

WebKit2GTK version mismatch on Linux

If you see errors like Package webkit2gtk-4.1 was not found, your distribution may ship an older WebKit2GTK version. Check which package is available:

apt-cache search webkit2gtk

Tauri 2.x requires webkit2gtk-4.1. If only webkit2gtk-4.0 is available, you may need to upgrade your distribution or compile WebKit2GTK from source.

Windows: error: linker link.exe not found

This means the MSVC build tools are not installed or not on your PATH. Re-run the Visual Studio Build Tools installer and ensure the "Desktop development with C++" workload is selected. Then restart your terminal.

Port conflicts when running npm run tauri dev

The Svelte dev server defaults to port 1420. If that port is in use, set a different port:

VITE_PORT=3000 npm run tauri dev

Make sure the Tauri configuration (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) also references the same port under build.devUrl.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: With DSCode installed and running, head to the Quick Start guide to learn the basics in under five minutes.

docs.title: Migrating from VS Code
docs.text: This guide walks you through migrating from Visual Studio Code to DSCode. DSCode is designed to feel familiar -- your keybindings, themes, snippets, and most extensions carry over directly.

docs.title: Step 1: Install DSCode
docs.text:
Download and install DSCode for your platform from the installation guide, or build from source:

macOSLinuxWindows

Download the .dmg from GitHub Releases and drag DSCode to Applications.

Install via .deb, .rpm, or .AppImage from GitHub Releases.

Run the .msi or .exe installer from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Step 2: Import Settings
docs.text:
DSCode uses the same settings.json format as VS Code. Copy your configuration files:

macOSLinuxWindows 
# VS Code settings location
# ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/

# Copy to DSCode
cp ~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/settings.json \
   ~/Library/Application\ Support/dscode/settings.json

cp ~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/keybindings.json \
   ~/Library/Application\ Support/dscode/keybindings.json

cp -r ~/Library/Application\ Support/Code/User/snippets/ \
   ~/Library/Application\ Support/dscode/snippets/

# VS Code settings location
# ~/.config/Code/User/

# Copy to DSCode
cp ~/.config/Code/User/settings.json ~/.config/dscode/settings.json
cp ~/.config/Code/User/keybindings.json ~/.config/dscode/keybindings.json
cp -r ~/.config/Code/User/snippets/ ~/.config/dscode/snippets/

# VS Code settings location
# %APPDATA%\Code\User\

# Copy to DSCode
Copy-Item "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\settings.json" "$env:APPDATA\dscode\settings.json"
Copy-Item "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\keybindings.json" "$env:APPDATA\dscode\keybindings.json"
Copy-Item -Recurse "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\snippets" "$env:APPDATA\dscode\snippets"

Unrecognized settings

Not all VS Code settings keys are recognized by DSCode yet. Unrecognized settings are silently ignored and will not cause errors. Core editor.*, workbench.*, terminal.*, and files.* settings have high compatibility.

docs.title: Step 3: Install Extensions
docs.text: DSCode uses the Open VSX Registry instead of the Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace. Most popular extensions are available on both, but some Microsoft-exclusive extensions may not be present.

docs.title: Check Extension Availability
docs.text:
List your VS Code extensions and check availability:

# Export your VS Code extension list
code --list-extensions > my-extensions.txt

# Review the list and search for each on Open VSX
cat my-extensions.txt

docs.title: Install Extensions
docs.text:
Install extensions one by one or use the CLI:

# Install from the marketplace
dscode --install-extension rust-lang.rust-analyzer
dscode --install-extension esbenp.prettier-vscode
dscode --install-extension dbaeumer.vscode-eslint

docs.title: Common Extension Mapping
docs.text: VS Code Extension Open VSX Availability Notes Python (ms-python) Available Full functionality Rust Analyzer Available Full functionality Prettier Available Full functionality ESLint Available Full functionality GitLens Available Core features work C/C++ (ms-vscode) Not available Use clangd instead Live Share Not available VS Code-exclusive GitHub Copilot Not compatible VS Code-specific API Remote SSH Not available DSCode remote development is planned Jupyter Available Extension host API works; frontend rendering incomplete

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Your Workspace
docs.text: Open your project in DSCode and verify key workflows:

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
If you have a .vscode/tasks.json, test that your tasks run correctly:

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P and type Tasks: Run Task.
  2. Select a task and verify it executes as expected.

docs.title: Debug Configurations
docs.text:
Test your .vscode/launch.json debug configurations:

  1. Open the Debug view (Ctrl+Shift+D).
  2. Select a configuration from the dropdown.
  3. Press F5 to start debugging.

Warning

Debug stepping (step over, step into, step out) is currently stubbed in DSCode. Breakpoints, continue, pause, and stop work correctly.

docs.title: Keybindings
docs.text:
Test your custom keyboard shortcuts:

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P and type Keyboard Shortcuts.
  2. Verify your custom bindings appear and work as expected.

docs.title: Key Architectural Differences
docs.text:
Understanding the differences helps set expectations:

Area VS Code DSCode Runtime Electron (bundled Chromium + Node.js) Tauri v2 (native webview + Rust) Memory usage 300-500 MB ~50 MB Cold start 1-3 seconds <100 ms Install size ~350 MB <30 MB Extension marketplace Microsoft Marketplace Open VSX Registry Extension API coverage 100% ~75% (targeting 95%+ for v1.0) Git backend Shells out to git CLI Native git2 Rust crate (no external binary) Terminal Built-in Node.js PTY portable-pty (Rust) + xterm.js Remote development Full (SSH, WSL, Containers, Tunnels) Not yet available (planned) Notebook support Full (Jupyter) Extension host API only; frontend incomplete Language servers Bundled via extensions 4 built-in (Python, Rust, Go, JSON) + extensions

docs.title: Common Issues and Workarounds
docs.text:
Extension fails to activate
  • Check the Extension Host log in the Output panel for API compatibility errors.
  • The extension may depend on VS Code APIs not yet implemented in DSCode. See the Compatibility Matrix.
  • Try an older version of the extension that may use fewer APIs.
Settings key not recognized
  • DSCode silently ignores unrecognized settings. If a feature is not working as expected, check whether the corresponding setting is supported.
  • Core editor, terminal, and file settings have high compatibility. Some workbench layout and advanced settings may differ.
Theme looks different
  • DSCode supports VS Code TextMate color themes. If colors appear slightly different, it may be due to differences in the webview rendering engine (WebKit/WebView2 vs. Chromium).
  • Workbench colors are fully supported. Token colors use the same TextMate grammar system.
Git pull fails with 'Merge required'
  • DSCode's built-in git pull only supports fast-forward merges. If your branch has diverged, use the integrated terminal to run git pull --rebase or git merge manually.
Extension requires Electron APIs
  • Extensions using require('electron') will not work. DSCode provides equivalent functionality through the vscode.env namespace.
  • Check if the extension has an Open VSX version that may have been adapted for non-Electron editors.

docs.text:
If you encounter issues during migration:

  • Search the docs -- Use the search bar at the top of this site.
  • Check the FAQ -- Common questions are answered in the FAQ.
  • Report issues -- File a bug report at GitHub Issues with the vscode-compat label.
  • Community -- Ask questions in GitHub Discussions.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get productive with DSCode in under five minutes. This guide walks you through the core workflows you will use every day.

docs.title: Launching DSCode
docs.text:
After installing DSCode, launch it from your terminal:

dscode .

Or open the application directly from your system launcher (Applications on macOS, application menu on Linux, Start Menu on Windows). If you are building from source, use cargo tauri dev to launch the development build.

When DSCode opens for the first time, you will see the Welcome tab with links to documentation, recent projects, and configuration options.

docs.title: Opening a Folder
docs.text:
DSCode is project-oriented -- most features work best when you have a folder open.

MenuKeyboardTerminal

Go to File > Open Folder... and select your project directory.

Press Ctrl+O (or Cmd+O on macOS) to open the folder picker.

Launch DSCode with a folder argument:

dscode /path/to/your/project

Once a folder is open, the Explorer sidebar displays the file tree on the left.

docs.title: Create a New File
docs.text:
1. Hover over the Explorer sidebar and click the New File icon, or
  2. Press Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) to create an untitled file.

docs.title: Basic Editing
docs.text:
DSCode uses the Monaco Editor -- the same editing engine behind VS Code. Everything you already know works here:

  • Undo / Redo -- Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z on macOS)
  • Save -- Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS)
  • Find -- Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on macOS)
  • Find and Replace -- Ctrl+H (Cmd+H on macOS)

For VS Code users

If you are coming from VS Code, your muscle memory transfers directly. DSCode mirrors the default VS Code keybindings, so shortcuts like Ctrl+D (select next occurrence) and Ctrl+Shift+L (select all occurrences) work the same way.

docs.title: The Command Palette
docs.text:
The Command Palette is the fastest way to access any command in DSCode.

Open it with Ctrl+Shift+P (or Cmd+Shift+P on macOS), then start typing to filter the list:

Try these commands to get started:

Type this... What it does theme Change the color theme settings Open user settings terminal Toggle the integrated terminal format document Auto-format the current file toggle word wrap Turn line wrapping on or off

Quick Open vs. Command Palette

Press Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) to open Quick Open, which searches for files by name instead of commands. Use this when you know the filename you want to jump to.

docs.title: The Integrated Terminal
docs.text:
Open the built-in terminal with Ctrl+` (Cmd+` on macOS), or through the Command Palette by typing Toggle Terminal.

The terminal opens at the root of your current workspace and supports:

  • Multiple terminal instances (click the + icon)
  • Split terminals (click the split icon or press Ctrl+Shift+5)
  • Shell selection (bash, zsh, PowerShell, etc.)

Running build commands

The integrated terminal is perfect for running build tools, test suites, and dev servers without leaving the editor. Try npm run dev, cargo build, or python app.py right inside DSCode.

docs.title: Installing an Extension
docs.text:
Extensions add language support, themes, debuggers, and more.

  1. Open the Extensions sidebar by clicking the extensions icon in the activity bar, or press Ctrl+Shift+X (Cmd+Shift+X on macOS).
  2. Search for an extension (for example, Python or Rust Analyzer).
  3. Click Install.

DSCode supports a wide range of VS Code-compatible extensions. See Installing Extensions for more details.

docs.title: Essential Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: These shortcuts will cover most of your daily editing needs:

docs.title: General
docs.text: Action Windows / Linux macOS Command Palette Ctrl+Shift+P Cmd+Shift+P Quick Open (file) Ctrl+P Cmd+P User Settings Ctrl+, Cmd+, Toggle Sidebar Ctrl+B Cmd+B Toggle Terminal Ctrl+` Cmd+` New Window Ctrl+Shift+N Cmd+Shift+N

docs.title: Editing
docs.text: Action Windows / Linux macOS Cut line Ctrl+X Cmd+X Copy line Ctrl+C Cmd+C Move line up/down Alt+Up / Alt+Down Option+Up / Option+Down Duplicate line Shift+Alt+Down Shift+Option+Down Delete line Ctrl+Shift+K Cmd+Shift+K Toggle comment Ctrl+/ Cmd+/ Multi-cursor ++alt+click++ ++option+click++ Select next occurrence Ctrl+D Cmd+D

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Action Windows / Linux macOS Go to line Ctrl+G Cmd+G Go to symbol Ctrl+Shift+O Cmd+Shift+O Go to definition F12 F12 Peek definition Alt+F12 Option+F12 Navigate back Alt+Left Ctrl+- Navigate forward Alt+Right Ctrl+Shift+-

Printable shortcut reference

For a comprehensive list, see the Keyboard Shortcuts Reference or press Ctrl+K then Ctrl+S (Cmd+K then Cmd+S on macOS) to open the interactive shortcut editor.

docs.title: Source Control Quick Start
docs.text:
DSCode has built-in Git support. Here is how to stage, commit, and diff in three steps:

  1. Open the Source Control view -- Press Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G on macOS) or click the branch icon in the Activity Bar.
  2. Stage changes -- Click the + icon next to changed files, or click + on the section header to stage all changes.
  3. Commit -- Type a commit message in the input box at the top of the SCM view and press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS).

Click any changed file in the SCM view to open a side-by-side diff showing exactly what has changed.

Tip

DSCode's Git is powered by the git2 Rust crate -- no external git binary is required. See the full Git Integration guide for details.

docs.title: Language Intelligence Quick Start
docs.text:
When you open a file in a supported language, DSCode automatically starts the appropriate language server and provides intelligent features:

  • Hover -- Hold your cursor over a symbol to see its type, documentation, and function signature.
  • Auto-completion -- Start typing to see context-aware suggestions. Press Ctrl+Space (Cmd+Space on macOS) to trigger completions manually.
  • Go to Definition -- Press F12 on a symbol to jump to its definition. Press Alt+F12 (Option+F12 on macOS) to peek at the definition inline.

DSCode ships with 4 built-in language servers (Python, Rust, Go, JSON). Install additional language extensions from the marketplace for other languages.

docs.title: Customization Quick Start
docs.text:
Make DSCode yours in under a minute:

  • Change theme -- Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and type Color Theme, then select from the list. Dark and light themes are available out of the box, and you can install more from the marketplace.
  • Adjust font size -- Open Settings (Ctrl+,) and search for editor.fontSize. Set it to your preferred size.
  • Customize keybindings -- Open the Command Palette and type Keyboard Shortcuts to browse and modify keybindings, or edit keybindings.json directly.

For VS Code users

DSCode reads the same settings.json and keybindings.json formats as VS Code. You can copy your existing configuration files to ~/.config/dscode/ (Linux), ~/Library/Application Support/dscode/ (macOS), or %APPDATA%\dscode\ (Windows) to get started immediately.

Key differences from VS Code:

  • DSCode uses the Open VSX marketplace instead of the Microsoft marketplace. Most popular extensions are available on both.
  • Remote development (SSH, WSL, containers) is not yet available.
  • Some VS Code-proprietary APIs are not implemented (~75% API coverage).
  • DSCode uses significantly less memory (~50 MB vs. 300-500 MB) and starts faster (<100ms vs. 1-3 seconds).

See Migrating from VS Code for a complete migration walkthrough.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Now that you know the basics, try building something! Head to Your First Project for a hands-on tutorial, or explore the User Guide for a deeper look at DSCode's features.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: DSCode provides a full-featured CLI for opening files, managing extensions, and controlling editor behavior from the terminal. After installation, the dscode binary is available on your PATH.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
dscode [options] [path...]

When invoked without arguments, DSCode opens the most recent workspace. When given one or more paths, it opens each file or folder in an editor window.

docs.title: Opening Files and Folders
docs.text:
Command Description dscode Open DSCode (restores the last session) dscode <file> Open a specific file in the editor dscode <folder> Open a folder as the workspace root dscode <file1> <file2> ... Open multiple files in tabs dscode <folder1> <folder2> ... Open a multi-root workspace 
# Open the current directory
dscode .

# Open a specific file
dscode src/main.rs

# Open multiple files
dscode index.html style.css app.js

# Open a multi-root workspace
dscode ~/projects/frontend ~/projects/backend

docs.title: Window Behavior
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --new-window -n Force a new window instead of reusing an existing one --reuse-window -r Reuse the most recently active window --wait -w Wait for the file to be closed before returning (useful for $EDITOR) --locale <locale> Set the display language (e.g., en, de, ja) 
# Always open in a new window
dscode --new-window ~/projects/my-app

# Reuse the existing window
dscode --reuse-window README.md

# Use DSCode as your git commit editor
git config --global core.editor "dscode --wait"

docs.title: File Navigation
docs.text:
Flag Description --goto <file>:<line>:<column> Open a file and place the cursor at the specified line and column --diff <file1> <file2> Open the diff editor comparing two files side by side 
# Open a file at line 42, column 10
dscode --goto src/main.rs:42:10

# Compare two files
dscode --diff old_config.json new_config.json

Shorthand goto syntax

You can also use the colon syntax directly without the --goto flag:

dscode src/main.rs:42:10

DSCode detects the file:line:col pattern automatically when a file path is given.

docs.title: Extension Management
docs.text:
Flag Description --install-extension <id-or-path> Install an extension by marketplace ID or .vsix file path --uninstall-extension <id> Uninstall an extension by its identifier --list-extensions List all installed extensions --show-versions Show extension versions when listing (use with --list-extensions) --force Skip confirmation prompts during install/uninstall 
# Install an extension from the marketplace
dscode --install-extension rust-lang.rust-analyzer

# Install from a local .vsix file
dscode --install-extension ~/downloads/my-extension-0.1.0.vsix

# Uninstall an extension
dscode --uninstall-extension rust-lang.rust-analyzer

# List all installed extensions with versions
dscode --list-extensions --show-versions

Example output from --list-extensions --show-versions:

esbenp.prettier-vscode@10.1.0
rust-lang.rust-analyzer@0.4.1894
svelte.svelte-vscode@108.3.1

docs.title: Informational Flags
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --version -v Print the DSCode version and exit --help -h Show the help message with all available flags --status -s Print process status and diagnostics --verbose Enable verbose logging to the terminal 
# Print version information
dscode --version
# Output: DSCode 0.1.0 (Tauri 2.x, commit abc1234)

# Show detailed process status
dscode --status

Example output from --status:

DSCode 0.1.0

Process Information:
  PID:            12345
  Uptime:         2h 15m
  Memory (RSS):   48 MB
  CPU:            0.3%

Extension Host:
  Status:         Running
  Extensions:     12 loaded
  PID:            12346
  Memory (RSS):   85 MB

Workspaces:
  /home/user/projects/my-app (active)

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
Flag Description --extensionDevelopmentPath <path> Load an extension in development mode from the given path --inspect-extensions <port> Attach a Node.js debugger to the extension host on the specified port --disable-extensions Start DSCode without loading any extensions --disable-gpu Disable GPU hardware acceleration --log <level> Set the log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error, off --user-data-dir <path> Override the user data directory --extensions-dir <path> Override the extensions installation directory --prof-startup Profile startup performance and write results to the console 
# Develop and test an extension
dscode --extensionDevelopmentPath ~/projects/my-extension

# Debug the extension host
dscode --inspect-extensions 9229

# Run without extensions (for troubleshooting)
dscode --disable-extensions

# Use a custom data directory (useful for isolated testing)
dscode --user-data-dir /tmp/dscode-test

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
DSCode reads the following environment variables to configure behavior at startup. All variables are optional; DSCode uses sensible defaults when they are not set.

Variable Default Description DSCODE_USER_DATA_DIR ~/.config/dscode (Linux), ~/Library/Application Support/dscode (macOS), %APPDATA%\dscode (Windows) Override the user data directory for settings, keybindings, and state DSCODE_EXTENSIONS_DIR <user-data-dir>/extensions Override the directory where extensions are installed DSCODE_LOG_LEVEL info Set the default log level (trace, debug, info, warn, error, off) DSCODE_DEV (unset) When set to 1, enables development mode with additional debug output DSCODE_DISABLE_GPU (unset) When set to 1, disables GPU hardware acceleration DSCODE_NNG_TIMEOUT 5000 Timeout in milliseconds for NNG IPC messages to the extension host DSCODE_FORCE_COLOR (unset) When set to 1, forces colored output in the terminal even without a TTY DSCODE_LOCALE System locale Override the display language (e.g., en, de, ja, zh-cn) EDITOR (unset) If set to dscode --wait, DSCode is used as the default editor for git and other CLI tools VISUAL (unset) Same as EDITOR, preferred by some Unix tools HTTP_PROXY (unset) HTTP proxy URL for marketplace and update requests HTTPS_PROXY (unset) HTTPS proxy URL for marketplace and update requests NO_PROXY (unset) Comma-separated list of hosts that bypass the proxy RUSTC_WRAPPER (unset) Used during builds from source (e.g., sccache for faster recompilation)

Setting environment variables permanently

macOS / Linux (bash/zsh)Windows (PowerShell)

Add to your shell profile (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, etc.):

export DSCODE_LOG_LEVEL="debug"
export DSCODE_EXTENSIONS_DIR="$HOME/.dscode-extensions"

Set persistent environment variables:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("DSCODE_LOG_LEVEL", "debug", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("DSCODE_EXTENSIONS_DIR", "$env:USERPROFILE\.dscode-extensions", "User")

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 General error 2 Invalid command-line argument 3 Extension install/uninstall failed 4 File or folder not found 5 Permission denied

docs.title: Shell Completion
docs.text:
DSCode can generate shell completion scripts for tab-completion support.

BashZshFishPowerShell 
dscode --generate-completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dscode

dscode --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_dscode
# Add to .zshrc: fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)

dscode --generate-completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dscode.fish

dscode --generate-completion powershell >> $PROFILE

docs.title: Use DSCode as your default $EDITOR
docs.text:
export EDITOR="dscode --wait"
export VISUAL="dscode --wait"

This lets tools like git commit, crontab -e, and kubectl edit open DSCode and wait for you to close the file before continuing.

docs.title: Pipe content into DSCode
docs.text:
# Open stdin in a new editor tab
echo "Hello, DSCode" | dscode -

# Pipe command output into the editor
kubectl logs my-pod | dscode -

docs.title: Diff two branches of a file
docs.text: dscode --diff <(git show main:config.json) <(git show feature:config.json)

docs.title: Profile startup performance
docs.text:
dscode --prof-startup
# Writes timing data to the console:
# [startup] Window ready: 68ms
# [startup] Extensions loaded: 142ms
# [startup] Workspace indexed: 210ms
